items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses the film 'Syncopation' and the musicians featured in it, but does not mention any personal interaction or professional relationship with director William Dieterle.

ctx.x: P R O C E E D I N G S

At the end of the last reel we were about to talk about the last film listed in 'Jazz in the Movies,' and that is, 'Syncopation,' 1942, directed by William Dieterle, a musical romance tracing in fictional form the development of jazz from 1906. Many musicians are featured including Benny Goodman, Charlie Barnet, Joe Venuti, Gene Krupa, Harry James, Rex Stewart, Alvino Rey, Jack Jenney, Connie Boswell, and the Hall Johnson Choir. Some sound track ghosting was done by Bunny Berygigan for Jackie Cooper, and by Stan…

Well, the basic group that you mentioned, we did the recording of that in New York. The picture was actually made in California, but the jam session sequence, which I presume is what this is all about, with Gene and all the people you mentioned there, we did that over at 20th Century Studios on 11th Avenue in New York. And this of course was sent out to Hollywood and incorporated in the picture. Because there were no dramatic roles involved in this at all.
